newsitem.title: CHILE: Quebrada Blanca miners, management in strike talks.
newsitem.headline: Quebrada Blanca miners, management in strike talks.

text.p: Unions and management at Chilean copper mine Quebrada Blanca will meet late Friday to try to close their wage contract talks after a three-day-old strike, union president Nelson Fuentes said.

The contract dispute centered on monthly salary levels, which Fuentes said are lower at Quebrada Blanca than at similar mines in northern Chile, but he sounded hopeful for chances of reaching a solution soon.
"We have some differences to work out, but we're confident we will be able to return to work as soon as possible," he told Reuters from the northern city of Iquique.
Talks are scheduled for late Friday afternoon in Iquique.
Company officials were not available for comment.
Fuentes said he was not sure what effect the strike had on production at the mine in Chile's arid First Region, but said Wednesday, when the strike began, that the pit was paralyzed.
The 75,000-tonne-a-year mine is owned by Cominco Ltd . Its roughly 300 unionized workers walked off the job when the current wage contract expired without a renewal.
